newsitem.title: USA: U.S. exercise machine companies settle with FTC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. exercise machine companies settle with FTC.

text.p: Four U.S. companies on Tuesday settled allegations with the Federal Trade Commission that they stretched weight-loss claims to entice customers to buy their exercise equipment.

The settlements were a part of the FTC's "Project Workout" campaign to crack down on exercise equipment makers and advertisers who were allegedly exaggerating the weight-loss benefits of their products.

Settlements were made with Carlsbad, California-based Abflex, U.S.A., Inc., which markets an abdominal exerciser under the same name, and Culver City, California-based Kent and Spiegel Direct, Inc., the infomercial production and distribution company responsible for the Abflex commercials.

Franklin Park, Illinois-based Life Fitness, which markets a variety of exercise equipment including the Lifecycle, a popular stationary bicycle, and Logan, Utah-based Icon Health and Fitness, Inc., which manufactures home exercise equipment including the Cross Walk Treadmill, also settled with the FTC.
"Consumers are likely to find ads that promise mega results for minimum effort extremely compelling," FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection Director Jodie Bernstein said.
The FTC said the companies could not back up the claims they made about weight-loss and spot reduction with concrete evidence.

Claims that users only needed to work out with the Abflex "Just 3 minutes a day" or that Lifecycle and Cross Walk Treadmill exercisers could burn about 1,000 calories in an hour were unsubstantiated, the agency said.

The proposed settlement agreements include prohibitions from making future claims without reliable evidence and an agreement that testimonials in commercials represent the typical experience of consumers.
